location_note: John has rebuilt the porch and changed that side of the garden. The new trial looks from the porch end towards the greenhouse, using the less-changed direction he identified.

sources.role: Greenhouse roof, bed and timber border from the same direction

prompt:
Create one single SQUARE, photorealistic documentary gardening photograph for John Lennon's UK book The Vegetable Guru. This is a first-photo-only location trial of John covering the grass with cardboard for his no-dig bed. Use the actual garden photograph #1 DSC01820 as the primary photographic plate for this image; reconstruct that very view, not an imagined garden. The real photographer is standing at the rebuilt porch end of the garden, looking AWAY FROM THE PORCH AND TOWARDS THE GREENHOUSE. The porch and its house-side features are behind or outside the picture. Composition aimed along the bed towards the greenhouses, slight diagonal as in 1. Do not mirror the scene, swing the camera to face the house, or show white porch windows, the porch-side water butts or anything rebuilt on that side. Bring the right-hand framing just inside the old foreground planter and large barrel in source 1 so the only foreground content is John, grass and cardboard. Keep the whole action independent of that changed edge. Upper third should be a quiet, identifiable background, cardboard and hands predominant.

Reference 1 is THE SAME CARDBOARD BED photographed during its real construction in March 2024. Its near short end crosses the lower foreground; its long axis runs diagonally up and right into the garden, stopping in front of the existing, low, timber-edged transverse vegetable bed in the distance. Keep the usable grassy strip immediately on the LEFT of the cardboard, and all cardboard on the actual bed footprint. Follow the real background positions and orientation: just left of the far end is the glazed aluminium greenhouse on its shallow masonry base. Its long glazed wall recedes towards the rear fence. A modest sliver of blue shed at far left through the gap or behind the panes if in shot; low weathered planter on short legs with bare berry canes on the grass in front, a few ordinary terracotta pots. Further back, low horizontal timber edging in front of the weathered pale horizontal fence and a little dark leafy kale. Reference 2 DSC01827 is the SAME bed later in the day from a few feet to the side, confirming greenhouse height, fence, footprint and the direction of the sightline. Retain the camera position and diagonal from #1. Use #2 ONLY to verify those landmarks. Do not copy any compost, wheelbarrow, rake or finished perimeter. Keep actual garden proportions. Natural candid, usable print photograph. Show enough of greenhouse structure to recognise the place without inventing extra greenhouses or moving the shed. Frame from the grass, a moderate lens, slight downward angle. Include a portion of real greenhouse roof for recognition within a square frame.

John is kneeling on the GRASS along the LEFT side of the near end, in three-quarter side view with body facing right towards the cardboard, both knees clear of the bed. His ungloved hands are actively laying the near edge of one plain flattened brown box onto another with a broad overlap. Head tipped gently down, realistic, relaxed posture. Put John in front of the left grassy strip with the greenhouse still visible above/beyond his shoulder, face and working hands both visible. Do not place the person on the narrow strip to the right of this bed or against the former porch. Barely visible wedge of freshly cut turf under the partly lowered sheet; the rest of the long bed has damp, slightly uneven overlapping box panels, a few large flattened cartons of subtly different brown tones. Show irregular creases, no labels, no print, no tape. A couple of loose pale pavers may sit on outer corners as in the source. Short, green, slightly patchy recently cut grass and a few broadleaf rosettes. No turned soil or compost in this new bed; living grass remains beneath. Only one gardener, one picture, no captions or panels.
Reference 3 is the real actor for face and clothing only. Match John in his olive knitted beanie, teal fleece jacket over dark jumper, work jeans and ordinary boots, without a microphone. His lowered face in reverse three-quarter is like the rightmost actual camera reference. Quite receding chin well behind his lower lip, short greying beard traces the underside of his jaw, nearly disappears into the collar. Keep John recognisable. Soft Cornish daylight, natural photographic textures. Do not transfer any background from the face reference. The greenhouse-facing view in the real site photo is the most important element.
